title: MUSCLE MANGA - Katsumi Orochi's Physique in Grappler Baki
summary: A Muscle Manga episode on Katsumi Orochi from Grappler Baki: his absurd childhood feats, his stats (185 cm, 115 kg, 300 kg bench, 10-second 100 m) and his thick, wide physique. NH uses the character to argue that muscular strength matters in combat as well as technique, and that talent gets you to the top but doesn't guarantee winning without the right mindset.
claims: Katsumi is depicted at 21 as 6 ft+, 115 kg, at most ~12% body fat, benching 300 kg and running 100 m in 10 seconds
Baki's author understands that thinking strength and weight advantages don't matter in combat is naive and dangerous; some muscular development is necessary
Pushing the limits of destructive ability requires becoming more powerful, which can't come from skill alone
Someone so gifted that he was jacked at 5 would make you want to quit bodybuilding too
A weighted one-arm handstand push-up from a dead bottom at 240 lb+ would be downright impossible for a real calisthenics athlete
Even superhumans have doubts and there is always a bigger dog
Bravado and arrogance can be a protection against demoralization
Being gifted at a sport doesn't make you the best; starting with the gifts lets you reach the top but doesn't guarantee it
Real combat experience, including defeat, is what reforms a talented fighter's mindset
